simple: A skybox is the big sky picture that surrounds your whole game world. It is made of six images folded into a giant cube around you, lined up so you cannot see the edges. The `Sky` object inside `Lighting` holds these images, plus the sun, moon, and stars, which rise and set with the time of day. A good skybox makes your world feel huge, like outer space or the bottom of the ocean.
analogy: A skybox is like the painted walls and ceiling of a giant room you stand in the middle of. If the paintings line up perfectly at the corners, it feels like an endless open sky instead of a box.
keyPoints: A skybox is a cube of six images: back, down, front, left, right, and up.
The images must line up seamlessly on every edge when folded into a cube.
To make one: insert a `Sky` object into `Lighting`, then set `SkyboxBk`, `SkyboxDn`, `SkyboxFt`, `SkyboxLf`, `SkyboxRt`, and `SkyboxUp` in the Properties window.
Import your own images to Roblox first before using them in a skybox.
The sun, moon, and stars rise and set based on `Lighting.ClockTime`.
Customize them with `SunTextureId`, `SunAngularSize`, `MoonTextureId`, `MoonAngularSize`, and `StarCount`. Turn them all off with `CelestialBodiesShown`.
`SkyboxOrientation` rotates the skybox using degrees for X, Y, and Z. It turns around Y first, then X, then Z.
Rotating the skybox does not move the sun, moon, stars, or dynamic clouds.

terms.skybox: Six images arranged as a huge cube around the world to make the sky.
terms.seamless: Lined up so perfectly you cannot see where one image ends and the next begins.
terms.panoramic: A wide, all-around view, like standing in the middle of a field and looking every direction.
terms.celestial bodies: Things in the sky like the sun, moon, and stars.
terms.angular size: How big something looks in the sky, measured in degrees. Setting it to 0 hides the sun or moon.
terms.texture: An image put on a surface, like a sky picture on one face of the skybox.
terms.orientation: Which way something is turned or tilted.
terms.axis: An imaginary line something spins around. Spinning around the Y axis keeps the horizon level, like a merry-go-round.
terms.modulo (%): The remainder after dividing. `370 % 360` is 10, which keeps an angle between 0 and 360.
terms.cubemap: A set of six images in a cube used for the sky or for reflections.

example.title: Slowly spin the sky
example.place: Script in ServerScriptService (add a Sky object to Lighting first)
example.code:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local sky = Lighting:WaitForChild("Sky")
local ROTATION_SPEED = 5 -- degrees per second

RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(deltaTime)
	sky.SkyboxOrientation = Vector3.new(
		30, -- keep a steady 30 degree tilt on X
		(sky.SkyboxOrientation.Y + ROTATION_SPEED * deltaTime) % 360, -- spin on Y
		0
	)
end)
explain: The script waits for the `Sky` object inside Lighting.
Every frame, `Heartbeat` gives `deltaTime`, the seconds since the last frame.
It adds 5 degrees per second to the Y angle, so the sky turns slowly like a merry-go-round.
`% 360` keeps the angle between 0 and 360 so the number never grows huge.
The X angle stays at 30, giving the sky a fixed tilt.

watchOut: Using images that do not line up at the edges. You will see seams where the cube faces meet.
Expecting the sun to spin with `SkyboxOrientation`. Only the six images rotate.
Forgetting to import your images first. They need asset IDs before you can use them.
Hiding the sun with `CelestialBodiesShown` when you only wanted it gone. That hides stars too; set `SunAngularSize` to 0 instead.
